nist.title: NIST SP 800-218A, Secure Software Development Practices for Generative AI and Dual-Use Foundation Models: An SSDF Community Profile (July 2024)

aima.title: OWASP AI Maturity Assessment (AIMA) Version 1.0, 11 August 2025

questions.text: Do your written security requirements cover your AI features, such as which models are allowed, what data they may see and what they may do?
questions.gap: Security requirements do not cover AI features

now.title: Write one page of AI security requirements
now.detail: List the models and providers you allow, the data each AI feature may see and the actions it may take. Add it to your existing requirements.

next.title: Check every AI feature against the requirements
next.detail: Review each live AI feature against the page and log the gaps as work items.

questions.text: Is one person accountable for the security of each AI feature, and have the people who build them had training on AI-specific attacks?
questions.gap: No named owner or AI security training for builders
questions.ok: Each AI feature has an owner and builders are trained

now.title: Name an owner for each AI feature
now.detail: Record the owner next to each feature in your register or backlog.

next.title: Train the builders on AI attacks
next.detail: Run a short session for everyone who writes prompts, pipelines or agent code. Cover prompt injection, data leakage and excessive agent permissions, and repeat it each year.

questions.text: Before you build or change an AI feature, do you threat model it for AI-specific attacks such as prompt injection, poisoned data and leaks through model output?
questions.gap: AI features are not threat modelled

now.title: Threat model your highest risk AI feature
now.detail: Pick the feature with the most sensitive data or the most autonomy. Map its inputs, retrieved content, tools and outputs, and list how each could be abused.

next.title: Make AI threat modelling part of design
next.detail: Add an AI threats section to your design template and require it for new features and for model or tool changes.

questions.text: Do you keep a record of the models, model versions, datasets, prompt templates and AI libraries each release uses?
questions.gap: No record of the models, data and prompts in each release
questions.ok: Each release records its models, data and prompts

now.title: Start an AI bill of materials
now.detail: For each AI feature, list the model and version, provider, datasets, vector stores, prompt templates and AI libraries. A spreadsheet is enough to start.

next.title: Produce the record with each release
next.detail: Generate the list from your build pipeline so it stays current, and keep it with the release.

questions.text: Before you adopt a third-party model, model API, embedding service or AI library, do you check its security, its terms on your data and where it came from?
questions.gap: Third-party models and AI libraries are not checked before use
questions.ok: Third-party models and AI libraries are checked before use

now.title: Review the providers you already use
now.detail: For each model provider and AI library, record the data terms, the retention and training settings, and the version you depend on.

next.title: Gate new AI components
next.detail: Require the same review before any new model, provider or AI library goes into a build, and scan downloaded model files before use.

questions.text: Are system prompts, prompt templates, agent tool definitions and model settings kept in version control and reviewed before they change, the same as code?
questions.gap: Prompts and model settings change without version control or review
questions.ok: Prompts and model settings are versioned and reviewed

now.title: Move prompts and model settings into version control
now.detail: Take system prompts, templates, tool definitions and settings out of dashboards and databases and into your repository.

next.title: Review prompt changes like code
next.detail: Require a second person to approve changes to prompts, tool definitions and model settings, with the same branch protection as code.

questions.text: Is the data you fine-tune on, evaluate with or retrieve from (RAG) checked for tampering, poisoning and sensitive content before use, with its source recorded?
questions.gap: Fine-tuning, evaluation or retrieval data is not checked before use
questions.ok: Data is checked and its source recorded before use
questions.nist_note: PW.3 covers training, testing, fine-tuning and aligning data. We apply it to retrieval data as well.

now.title: Record where each dataset and document source comes from
now.detail: List the sources for fine-tuning, evaluation and retrieval, who can add to them, and which have no known origin.

next.title: Check data before it goes in
next.detail: Add checks for injected instructions, personal information and unexpected changes before data is used for fine-tuning or added to a retrieval index.

questions.text: Are model weights, fine-tuning data, vector stores and model provider API keys protected with least-privilege access and kept out of code?
questions.gap: Model keys, data or weights are not locked down
questions.ok: Model keys, data and weights have least-privilege access

now.title: Move model API keys into a secrets store
now.detail: Remove keys from code, notebooks and config files, rotate any that were exposed, and give each environment its own key.

next.title: Tighten access to AI data and models
next.detail: Limit who and what can read or change vector stores, fine-tuning data and model files, and review the access list each quarter.

questions.text: Do you validate what goes into the model and what comes out, and limit what agents and tools are allowed to do?
questions.help: For example input filtering, encoding output before it is shown or run, tool allow lists and a person approving risky actions.
questions.gap: Model inputs, outputs and agent actions are not constrained
questions.ok: Model inputs, outputs and agent actions are constrained

now.title: Limit what your agents and tools can do
now.detail: Give each AI feature the narrowest tool and data permissions it needs, and require a person to approve actions that send, pay, delete or publish.

next.title: Treat model output as untrusted input
next.detail: Encode or validate output before it is shown, stored or run, and filter inputs and retrieved content for injected instructions.

questions.text: Before release, do you test AI features for attacks such as prompt injection, jailbreaks, data leakage and misuse of tools, not only for answer quality?
questions.ok: AI features are tested for attacks before release

now.title: Run a first adversarial test
now.detail: Spend a day attacking your highest risk feature with known prompt injection and data leakage cases, and log what you find as defects.

next.title: Automate the attack cases
next.detail: Turn the cases into an automated test set that runs in your pipeline, and add new cases when you find new issues.

questions.text: When you change a model, model version, prompt or data source, do you re-run security and quality evaluations against set pass criteria before it goes live?
questions.gap: AI changes go live without set pass criteria
questions.ok: AI changes pass set evaluations before going live

now.title: Write down pass criteria for AI changes
now.detail: Agree the evaluations a model, prompt or data change must pass, and the results that block a release.

next.title: Block releases that fail the criteria
next.detail: Run the evaluations automatically on every AI change, including model version updates from your provider, and stop the release when they fail.

questions.text: Are development, evaluation and production separated for your AI features, with production data and keys kept out of development and testing?
questions.gap: Production data or keys are used in development
questions.ok: Development, evaluation and production are separated

now.title: Take production data out of development
now.detail: Find where real customer data or production keys are used in notebooks, test prompts or development vector stores, and replace them.

next.title: Separate the environments
next.detail: Give development, evaluation and production their own accounts, keys and data stores.

questions.text: In production, do you log and watch model inputs, outputs, tool calls and usage for misuse and unusual behaviour?
questions.gap: Model inputs, outputs and tool calls are not monitored
questions.ok: Model inputs, outputs and tool calls are monitored
questions.nist_note: PO.5.3 is written for development environments. The AIMA Event Management practice covers production.

now.title: Log AI inputs, outputs and tool calls
now.detail: Keep the logs behind access controls with a set retention period, and mask personal information you do not need.

next.title: Alert on misuse
next.detail: Set alerts for spikes in usage or cost, injection patterns and unusual tool calls, and name who responds.

questions.text: Can users and researchers report AI security issues to you, and do you triage and fix them, including issues in the model itself?
questions.gap: No route to report or fix AI security issues
questions.ok: AI security issues can be reported and are fixed

now.title: Publish a way to report AI issues
now.detail: Add AI behaviour and model issues to your security contact page or vulnerability disclosure policy.

next.title: Add AI to your incident process
next.detail: Define how you triage AI reports, who decides, and how you fix and confirm a model, prompt or data issue.

questions.text: Can you quickly switch off an AI feature or roll back to an earlier model, prompt or data version, and have you agreed when you would?
questions.gap: No quick way to switch off or roll back an AI feature
questions.ok: AI features can be switched off or rolled back

now.title: Add a switch to turn off each AI feature
now.detail: Make sure each AI feature can be turned off or moved to a fallback without a code release.

next.title: Agree when to stop or roll back
next.detail: Write the conditions that trigger a stop or roll back, keep earlier model, prompt and index versions available, and test a roll back once.
